answer: Roof-inspection mills used to certify 40 empty warehouses from a single desk photo. A certificate now posts only after the inspector hangs a 2.1-kg optical prism from the documented vertex of bay 7, records an 18-minute solar caustic that passes through the hollow of the truss onto a painted floor datum, and files the image hash plus a 37-km odometer log. If the caustic angle misses the datum by more than 2.5 degrees, or the prism pouch returns unused, the bond is slashed and the claim is void.
